_comment: The CAD, G-vii task 3b - the mod's FIRST 3D model. Nothing in either gate renders a frame
(ai/LESSONS.md L41), so every visual claim here is smoke steps 10-14's to settle.
flip_v is TRUE because this OBJ's V is bottom-up: with it false, 32% of the faces sample the
texture's black background instead of its paint. Measured, not assumed.
automatic_culling is FALSE because it culls quads lying on a block boundary - a block's
concern. On an item it can only ever punch an invisible hole.
render_type is cutout because the emissive mask's alpha is 0 or 255 and nothing between.
The transform brings a mesh authored in 0-16 pixel space onto the block and centres it; the
THE HAND ROTATIONS ARE +90, NOT VANILLA HANDHELD'S -90. Vanilla's block item uses
firstperson_righthand [0,45,0] to show a cube's front AND right faces, which is only true if
+Z points at the PLAYER in hand space - the same way round as the GUI camera. Ry(-90) would
therefore send this model's +X muzzle to +Z, straight at the player's face, which is what the
first smoke round reported. The lefthand entries are the righthand ones with y and z negated,
because ItemTransform.apply negates them AGAIN at runtime; that is vanilla's own convention.
Their TRANSLATIONS are identical to the righthand ones on purpose - apply() flips only the sign
of translation.x for the left hand, so writing the mirror here would mirror it twice.
The gui and fixed translations and scales are SOLVED by ai/tools/cad_model.py, not typed: the
model is centred and fitted to its slot, so it cannot bleed into the next one.
